questions.text: Please provide a brief description of your company and the primary services you deliver to our organization.
questions.helper: Include year founded, employee count, and primary service lines.

questions.text: What is the primary nature of your engagement with our organization?
questions.helper: Select the option that best describes your service role.

questions.text: Is your service cloud-based, on-premises, service-based (no software component), or a hybrid?
Have you undergone any security assessment, audit, or third-party review in the past 24 months?
questions.evidence: Most recent audit report or executive summary
questions.helper: Examples: SOC 2 Type II, penetration test, ISO 27001 audit.

questions.text: Do you have a dedicated security or privacy function (security team, CISO, privacy officer, or equivalent)?
Do you maintain a written information security policy that is reviewed at least annually?
questions.evidence: Information security policy (executive summary or table of contents)

questions.text: What categories of data will your service create, access, process, transmit, or store on behalf of our organization?
questions.helper: Select all that apply.

questions.text: Do you store our organization's data on your systems or infrastructure?
In what country or countries is our organization's data stored and processed?
questions.helper: Include all storage and processing locations, including backup sites.

questions.text: Do you have a formal data classification policy that governs how different types of data are handled and protected?
How do you ensure that our organization's data is logically separated from other customers' data?
questions.helper: Describe your multi-tenant isolation controls if applicable.

questions.text: Do you have a documented process for returning or destroying our data at contract termination?
Have you experienced a data breach, unauthorized access, or security incident involving customer data in the past three years?
questions.helper: If yes, provide a summary of what occurred and corrective actions taken.

questions.text: Do you share our organization's data with any third parties other than your disclosed subprocessors?
Is multi-factor authentication (MFA) required for all workforce members who access systems holding our data?
questions.helper: MFA means a second factor beyond a password, such as an authenticator app or hardware key.

questions.text: Do you enforce a least-privilege access model, limiting user permissions to only what is needed for their role?
How is user access to our data or systems approved, reviewed, and revoked?
questions.helper: Describe the process from onboarding through offboarding.

questions.text: Do you conduct periodic access reviews (at minimum annually) to verify that access rights are still appropriate?
Do privileged or administrator accounts receive additional controls such as separate credentials, session recording, or just-in-time access?
questions.helper: Privileged accounts include system admins, database admins, and anyone with elevated system access.

questions.text: Do you use a password policy that enforces minimum length, complexity, and rotation requirements?
Is remote access to your internal systems controlled through a VPN or equivalent secure channel?
Do you log all access to systems and data that contain our organization's information?
Is our organization's data encrypted in transit (e.g., using TLS 1.2 or higher)?
questions.helper: Encryption in transit protects data as it moves between systems or users.

questions.text: Is our organization's data encrypted at rest?
questions.helper: Encryption at rest protects stored data files, databases, and backups.

questions.text: What encryption standards or algorithms do you use for data at rest and in transit?
questions.helper: Examples: AES-256, TLS 1.3. Provide the standard used for each.

questions.text: How are encryption keys managed and protected?
questions.helper: Describe key generation, rotation, storage, and access controls.

questions.text: Are encryption keys stored separately from the data they protect?
questions.helper: Storing keys alongside encrypted data significantly weakens the protection.

questions.text: Do your backup copies follow the same encryption requirements as production data?
Do you follow a secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) that includes security review or testing before release?
Do you conduct vulnerability scanning or penetration testing of your systems at least annually?
questions.evidence: Most recent penetration test summary or remediation report

questions.text: Do you have a formal change management process that requires review and testing of changes before deployment to production?
Do you apply security patches and software updates within a defined timeframe following release?
questions.helper: Describe your patching SLA for critical, high, and medium vulnerabilities.

questions.text: Do you maintain a vulnerability disclosure or bug bounty program?
Do you maintain a documented incident response plan?
What is your process for notifying customers in the event of a security incident affecting their data?
questions.helper: Include the communication channel, point of contact, and typical timeline.

questions.text: What is your target timeline for notifying customers of a confirmed data breach?
questions.helper: Specify hours or days from confirmation of incident.

questions.text: Do you maintain audit logs of system and data access, and are those logs protected from tampering?
How long are audit and security logs retained?
questions.helper: Specify the retention period in months or years.

questions.text: Do you conduct tabletop or live incident response exercises at least annually?
Do you use a security information and event management (SIEM) system or equivalent for real-time threat detection?
Do you maintain regular data backups for systems that hold our organization's data?
What is your target recovery time objective (RTO) for restoring services after a critical outage?
questions.helper: RTO is the maximum acceptable time to restore normal operations after an incident.

questions.text: What is your target recovery point objective (RPO) — that is, how much data loss is acceptable in a worst-case scenario?
questions.helper: RPO is the maximum age of data that must be recovered. Example: 4 hours means up to 4 hours of data could be lost.

questions.text: Are backups tested regularly to confirm they can be successfully restored?
Do you maintain a documented business continuity or disaster recovery plan?
questions.evidence: Business continuity or DR plan (executive summary)

questions.text: Have you tested your disaster recovery procedures in the past 12 months?
Do you use a third-party cloud provider (such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud) to host your service?
questions.helper: If yes, name the provider(s) and describe your shared responsibility model.

questions.text: Are your hosting environments certified or compliant with recognized security standards (e.g., SOC 2, FedRAMP, ISO 27001)?
questions.evidence: Hosting provider compliance documentation or shared compliance report

questions.text: Do you use network segmentation to isolate production systems from development, testing, and administrative systems?
Do you use firewalls, intrusion detection, or intrusion prevention systems to protect your infrastructure?
Do you have a process for managing and inventorying hardware and software assets?
Is your infrastructure monitored continuously for availability and performance?
Are all devices used by your workforce to access our data required to have endpoint protection software (antivirus, EDR)?
Are mobile devices that access your systems subject to mobile device management (MDM) controls?
questions.helper: MDM allows remote wipe and enforces device-level security policies.

questions.text: Do you enforce full-disk encryption on laptops and portable devices?
Do you have a policy governing the use of personal (BYOD) devices for work purposes?
Are USB or removable media restricted or controlled on devices that access sensitive data?
Do you conduct security awareness training for all workforce members at least annually?
Do all workforce members with access to our data complete training before being granted access?
Do you conduct background checks on employees and contractors who will have access to our data?
Do you have acceptable use policies covering workforce member behavior with respect to data and systems?
Are terminated employees' access rights revoked immediately upon departure?
Do you conduct role-specific security training for personnel with elevated access or technical responsibilities?
Do you use subcontractors or subprocessors to deliver any part of your service to our organization?
Do any subcontractors or subprocessors have access to our organization's data?
How do you assess and monitor the security practices of your subcontractors?
questions.evidence: Subcontractor security assessment process or sample vendor questionnaire

questions.text: Are your subcontractors contractually required to meet the same security and privacy standards as your own organization?
Will you provide us with a list of subcontractors or subprocessors that may access our data?
Do you notify customers of material changes to your subprocessor list before those changes take effect?
Do you hold any current security or privacy certifications (e.g., SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HITRUST)?
questions.evidence: Certification report or letter of attestation

questions.text: Are those certifications current and within their renewal window?
Are you willing to share audit reports, SOC 2 reports, or equivalent documentation under a non-disclosure agreement?
Do you conduct or commission annual internal or external security risk assessments?
questions.evidence: Risk assessment summary or scope statement

questions.text: Do you have a process for identifying, tracking, and remediating compliance findings or audit observations?
Do you have a documented privacy policy that covers how you handle customer data?
What is your data retention schedule for our organization's data?
questions.helper: Specify how long data is kept in active systems, archives, and backups.

questions.text: Do you have a process for responding to data subject access requests or data deletion requests?
Are you able to confirm the specific locations where our data is stored, including any geographies outside the United States?
Do you use our organization's data for any secondary purposes, such as analytics, benchmarking, or product improvement?
questions.helper: If yes, describe what data is used and how it is de-identified or protected.

questions.text: Do you qualify as a Business Associate under HIPAA based on the services you will provide?
questions.helper: A Business Associate is any vendor that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits PHI on behalf of a Covered Entity.

questions.text: Are you willing to sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) before PHI is shared with your organization?
questions.helper: A signed BAA is required by HIPAA before PHI may be shared with a Business Associate.

questions.text: Is PHI encrypted both at rest and in transit in your systems?
Do all workforce members who may access PHI receive HIPAA training before access is granted and at least annually thereafter?
questions.evidence: Training completion records or training policy

questions.text: Do you maintain audit logs specific to PHI access, including who accessed what data and when?
questions.helper: HIPAA requires audit controls that record and examine activity in systems containing PHI.

questions.text: What is your breach notification timeline for incidents involving PHI?
questions.helper: HIPAA requires notification to a Covered Entity without unreasonable delay and within 60 days of discovery.

questions.text: Do you conduct and document periodic security risk assessments covering PHI as required by the HIPAA Security Rule?
Do your subcontractors that may access PHI also sign a Business Associate Agreement?
questions.evidence: Subcontractor BAA policy or sample agreement

questions.text: Is access to PHI limited to the minimum necessary information required to perform the contracted service?
questions.helper: The HIPAA minimum necessary standard requires limiting PHI access to what is needed to accomplish the intended purpose.

questions.text: Can you confirm where PHI will be stored and processed, including cloud regions and any non-US locations?
Do you have documented policies and procedures for HIPAA compliance that are reviewed and updated at least annually?
questions.evidence: HIPAA policy index or table of contents

questions.text: Will you accept contractual security and privacy obligations, including the right to audit?
Do you carry cyber liability or errors and omissions insurance?
questions.helper: Specify coverage amounts if available.

questions.text: Are you currently subject to any pending legal actions, regulatory investigations, or known material compliance violations?
What is your policy for data breach liability and indemnification?
Are you willing to provide annual security attestations or questionnaire updates during the contract term?
